brief.headline: Continuity Guardian escalated
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 1664747 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_month_end_close, idle in transaction, txn open 4.2s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 28% over 30s (87/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $13,340/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_month_end_close, pid 1664747) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $13,340/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Both terminating and waiting exceed the 60s business degradation tolerance. Terminating triggers a 95-minute replay cost (BIZ-2, BIZ-5) with policy=consult_owner (BIZ-5, CHG-4410). Waiting costs ~$799,466 in lost checkout revenue and EXCEEDS the 60s tolerance (BIZ-4). The active change-calendar window CHG-4410 requires owner escalation per I3. No candidate action is viable without owner decision.

audit.report: The month-end close job (batch_replayable_month_end_close) blocked checkout sessions, causing 27 timeouts and a 55% success rate over 15 seconds. The blocking transaction had been idle for only 4.2 seconds in a read-only SELECT 1 state. Both waiting and terminating the blocker exceeded the business's 60-second degradation tolerance: waiting incurred approximately $799,466 in lost checkout revenue over the extended period, while terminating triggered a mandatory 95-minute inventory replay. The case was escalated to finance-ops for owner decision.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_month_end_close transaction held locks that caused checkout sessions to timeout, and the guardians could not resolve the trade-off between waiting for natural lock release and terminating into a costly replay without owner escalation.
lessons: For batch_replayable_month_end_close, verify the change-calendar (CHG-4410) and interrupt policy before a lock-contention incident; the policy=consult_owner requires finance-ops approval before any terminate/wait decision can be safe.

Instrument the batch_replayable_month_end_close job to surface its estimated remaining runtime and interruptibility status in the workload registry, so future guardians can compute revenue-at-risk in real time without relying on post-hoc probes.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian proposed three rounds (wait, wait, escalate), each time correctly identifying that both terminating and waiting violated the 60s business tolerance, but the process stalled because the continuity guardian required change-calendar evidence that was not initially provided, forcing a third escalation round.
follow_ups: Contact finance-ops to confirm the interrupt policy for batch_replayable_month_end_close and document the escalation path for future lock-contention events.
Add a pre-incident checklist to the runbook: verify change-calendar status and workload registry interrupt flags for all batch_replayable jobs before the month-end close window.
Configure automated alerts when checkout success drops below 95% for 10 seconds, directly routing to the finance-ops owner to avoid multi-round guardian negotiation.
